issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes with snake_case names (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all methods reference camelCase names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This name mismatch causes compilation errors and contradicts the UML and problem description which use camelCase attribute names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute names consistent with the UML and method usages. For example, rename the declared fields in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or update all constructor and method references to match the declared snake_case names. Ensure the constructor, getters, setters and other methods use the same field identifiers so the class compiles and matches the problem specification.

issues.description: The UML and task description use camelCase attribute names (e.g. lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implementation declares the same conceptual attributes using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while its constructor and methods refer to the camelCase names. This mismatch creates a clear naming inconsistency across problem statement, template expectation, and solution code, making it hard for students to map requirements to implementation and causing compile/runtime confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Align attribute identifiers across all artifacts. Rename the solution's fields to the camelCase names used in the UML and methods (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), or alternatively rename constructor parameters and all methods to consistently use the snake_case field names. Prefer using the camelCase names to match the problem statement and Java naming conventions.
